market.domesticSlice: India-specific figures; drone regulation (DGCA) and government procurement make this largely a domestic-policy-driven market

structureFacts: India's drone market is growing at a healthy ~8.45% CAGR, with real government policy support: a proposed PLI 2.0 scheme (~₹1,000 crore) targeting 30% local drone production, on top of an existing ₹120 crore PLI allocation for drone/UAS manufacturing.

The market's most-cited major players (ideaForge, Garuda Aerospace, Asteria Aerospace) are primarily drone HARDWARE/manufacturing companies — a different business model and a different competitive tier from a drone-data/analytics-only SaaS company like Kesowa.

Skylark Drones is the closer business-model analog to Kesowa — a drone-data-and-analytics services company rather than a hardware manufacturer — and is the more meaningful peer comparison even though it is not itself independently sized here.

Government/PSU procurement (municipal corporations, pollution control boards, coal/mining PSUs) is a real, recurring demand channel for drone-survey services in India, distinct from the consumer/hobbyist or defense segments of the broader drone market.

adoptionStructure.note: A project/contract-based B2B and B2G (business-to-government) services model — survey/mapping engagements and SaaS platform access, not a subscription-only or hardware-sale model.

drivers: Speed and safety versus manual survey methods — e.g. avoiding a dangerous manual walk-through of an unstable mine haul road after heavy rain.
Government/PSU trust built through direct project delivery (municipal corporations, pollution control boards, coal-mining subsidiaries) rather than broad brand marketing.
Data usability (organized, analyzable geospatial output) rather than raw imagery alone — the actual value-add of a software/analytics layer over a drone flight.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Delivered project outcomes with real government/PSU counterparties — in a B2G services model, one credible, specific case study (like a named mine-safety survey) does more for the next contract than broad platform feature claims.

steps: identify buyer (government/PSU agency or corporate client with a survey/monitoring need)
scope the specific survey/mapping/monitoring problem
win via prior project credibility and price
deliver via drone survey + ARU platform analytics
maintain the ARU Skynet software platform (upload, organize, analyze, collaborate)
develop/maintain AI models (Tree Count AI, Visual Pollution Index)
coordinate drone flight operations (own team and/or partner pilots — not independently confirmed which)
produce client deliverables (3D models, imagery, analysis reports)
plan drone flights against project scope and site access
capture aerial imagery/data on-site
process and upload data via the ARU platform
deliver analyzed output to the client
onboard client (government tender or direct engagement)
execute the survey/monitoring project
deliver analysis and support interpretation
pursue repeat/expanded engagements with the same agency
demand arises from a specific government/PSU monitoring or safety need
project scoped and won (often via tender)
fulfil via drone survey + platform analytics
recurring/repeat engagement if the relationship holds
